explanation: Two users interacting on the same system, at the same time, without interference.

tagline.text: Duo Input lets staff and customers use separate displays at the same time. One system keeps running, while each person gets the input space they need.

info-1.title: Built for one. Used by two
info-1.paragraph1: Customer-facing systems often need two people to work at once: staff keeping the case moving, and a customer entering details, confirming choices or signing.
info-1.paragraph2: Most operating systems still treat that as one shared input session. The cursor jumps, focus moves, and one person interrupts the other.
info-1.paragraph3: That creates waiting, repeated instructions and awkward handoffs in moments where the experience should feel calm and professional.

info-2.title: Each screen gets its own session
info-2.paragraph1: Duo Input handles multiple input sources independently at system level, below the application layer.
info-2.paragraph2: The service screen stays usable while the customer screen receives its own touch, typing or signature input.
info-2.paragraph3: One workflow can stay visible across two displays, while each person interacts with the part of the process meant for them.

info-3.title: The company that solved it
info-3.paragraph1: Forms, confirmations and digital signatures can happen in parallel with staff work instead of stopping it.
info-3.paragraph2: The technology is patented, built by ID24 and intended for real environments where shared systems need reliable multi-display input.
info-3.paragraph3: From service counters to signing workflows, Duo Input makes two-user interaction feel like one continuous experience.
